description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:84-92

```rust
/// Type of a change recorded in the in-memory change log.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum ChangeType {
    /// Object was created.
    Created,
    /// Object was updated.
    Updated,
    /// Object was destroyed.
    Destroyed,
}
```

This type is re-exported through `tests/common/mod.rs:15` and
documented in the test helper module as part of the consumer-facing
surface. Two contract problems:

1. **Missing `#[non_exhaustive]`.** A future variant — e.g. `Moved`
   if JMAP FileNode ever grows a stable-id move-with-rename operation,
   or `SoftDeleted` for trash-with-undo — would be a SemVer-breaking
   change. The fix is one annotation now; deferring it costs every
   downstream `match ChangeType` site at the next minor bump.

2. **Canonical-template divergence.** `jmap-mail-server` (the canonical
   extension-server template per workspace AGENTS.md) does NOT export
   a `ChangeType` enum:
   `grep -n "pub.*enum" crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs` returns
   nothing. The canonical sibling tracks changes via a private internal
   enum (or equivalent) and never exposes it.

   Per the propagation rule in `crate-jmap-filenode-server/AGENTS.md`:
   "if you reshape this crate in a way that diverges from
   jmap-mail-server, change jmap-mail-server first, then propagate."
   This crate added a public type that the canonical does not have.
   Either the canonical needs it (and the change starts there) or
   filenode-server should make it `pub(crate)`.

The simplest fix is to make `ChangeType` `pub(crate)` (it is only
used internally for the BFS in the change log and externally only by
the integration tests' `common` module, which can be re-routed
through another seam). This eliminates both problems and removes
one tile of cookie-cutter divergence.

If the type genuinely needs to be public — e.g. so downstream
backend authors building their own change log can mirror the
reference impl — then it MUST be `#[non_exhaustive]`. The current
state is the worst of both: public with no protection against
additive evolution.
title: pub enum ChangeType lacks #[non_exhaustive] AND has no equivalent in canonical jmap-mail-server
